text: Leading a team effectively requires a blend of skills, but a few stand out. Clear communication is the foundation, ensuring everyone understands their tasks and the project's goals. Equally important is delegation—assigning work based on each member's strengths, rather than doing everything yourself. Regular, constructive feedback helps people improve, while public recognition fuels motivation. When disagreements arise, address them quickly and calmly, focusing on the issue rather than blaming individuals. A good leader listens, guides, and creates a safe space for honest discussion, which turns potential conflicts into opportunities for stronger collaboration. Remember, a team succeeds when its members feel heard and valued.
